recent_posts.title: How freelance designers can scale their workflow using Webflow Foundations
recent_posts.summary: Freelance designers often face a visibility-to-delivery gap where growing demand outpaces their ability to deliver efficiently. Webflow Foundations, part of the Webflow Partner Program, is presented as a solution that enables a system-driven approach using reusable components, design tokens, and consistent layouts. By investing in a personal design system once, freelancers can reduce setup time, eliminate repetitive rework, and scale their practice. The Dribbble and Webflow combination is framed as a unified workflow: Dribbble for visibility and client acquisition, Webflow Foundations for systemized, repeatable delivery.

recent_posts.title: Dribbble and Framer partner to offer expert badge and 30% discount for qualified designers
recent_posts.summary: Dribbble has partnered with Framer to create a verified Framer Experts program for designers who build production-ready websites. Recognized experts get a badge boosting visibility in Designer Search, a dedicated landing page listing, and an exclusive 30% discount on Framer's annual plan. The program targets designers who own the full workflow from concept to launch, helping them attract higher-quality inbound clients and establish authority in the design-to-development space.

recent_posts.title: The golden age of women’s sports branding is here, and designers are leading it.
recent_posts.summary: Women's sports are experiencing a branding renaissance, and designers are at the center of it. From the Toronto Tempo's WNBA expansion jerseys to personality-driven sports media concepts and lifestyle merchandise, visual identity in women's sports has evolved beyond logos and uniforms into full cultural ecosystems. Brands are investing in digital-first, community-driven identities, creating demand for identity designers, motion designers, apparel specialists, and social-native creatives. Dribbble showcases this shift through concept work that blends editorial typography, expressive illustration, and experiential branding across retail, hospitality, and digital spaces.

recent_posts.title: Designing their own paths: Women in the Dribbble community share their stories
recent_posts.summary: For International Women's Day, several women designers and creative leaders from the Dribbble community share their personal stories about building careers in design. Themes include freelancing without a roadmap, running studios, supporting women-led businesses, balancing motherhood with creative work, and trusting one's own voice. Contributors include illustrators, studio founders, and brand designers from various backgrounds, each describing how they've shaped their careers on their own terms.

recent_posts.title: How to post work on Dribbble to attract the right clients
recent_posts.summary: A practical guide for designers on how to effectively share work on Dribbble to attract clients. Covers what types of work belong on the platform, how to maintain a consistent posting rhythm (1-2 shots per week), how to craft compelling shots with clear titles, descriptions, and tags, and how to optimize a profile to convert visitors into clients. Includes a pre-publish checklist.

recent_posts.title: Designing in Public, Thinking Long‑Term, and Growing With Dribbble
recent_posts.summary: Eugene, Design Lead at Shakuro, shares how his team uses Dribbble as a creative engine for experimentation and growth. Over years of consistent posting, Dribbble evolved from a closed community into a platform that attracts long-term clients and shapes the team's design thinking. The team prioritizes quality over quantity, uses the platform to explore ideas freely, and builds trust through consistent, intentional work. Skills from 3D and motion design inform their product work, while their focus on clarity and accessibility defines their approach. Dribbble serves both as a creative space and a client filter, enabling relationships that span years rather than single projects.

recent_posts.title: How to evaluate website build quality beyond visual design
recent_posts.summary: Build quality in websites is harder to spot than visual design but determines long-term maintainability. Key indicators include reusable component libraries, global styling systems, logical class naming, scalable CMS architecture, and optimized performance. Well-built sites become easier to maintain over time through systematic approaches, while poorly built sites require frequent rebuilds despite looking good initially. Critical evaluation questions focus on component systems, handoff documentation, CMS structure, and scalability planning.

recent_posts.title: Five challenges shaping the future of product and packaging design
recent_posts.summary: Modern design faces five key challenges: creating multi-sensory experiences beyond visual appeal, moving from 2D to spatial thinking, enabling real-time collaboration instead of sequential feedback loops, reducing physical prototyping waste while maintaining creative freedom, and exploring beyond conventional use cases. Digital 3D visualization tools are emerging to address these challenges by making complex surface effects explorable before production, enabling dynamic stakeholder collaboration, and reducing unnecessary physical samples. The shift represents design becoming more experiential and collaborative even when final outputs are physical products.

recent_posts.title: How to implement micro interactions in WordPress using visual tools
recent_posts.summary: Micro interactions are subtle animations that guide users through websites by providing visual cues and feedback. The article explains the four key elements (trigger, rules, feedback, loops/modes) and demonstrates how to implement five specific micro interactions in WordPress using the Droip website builder: responsive button interactions, scroll tracking progress bars, spring transitions, cursor trail effects, and animated text reveals. Each implementation is explained step-by-step without requiring code, using visual tools like the Animation Library, Visual Interaction Builder, and Element States. Best practices emphasize subtlety, user intent, brand consistency, and cross-device testing.

recent_posts.title: How Nixtio Built a Global Design Studio with Flexibility, Feedback, and a Whole Lot of Dribbble
recent_posts.summary: Nixtio, a global design studio with team members in Miami, Valencia, and roots in Ukraine, shares their 13-year journey building a multidisciplinary practice through Dribbble. The studio credits consistent daily publishing, active use of Dribbble's marketplace features, and community engagement for their growth. They emphasize adaptability over signature style, turning early harsh client feedback into motivation, and maintaining consistency as their key to success. The team plans to share more behind-the-scenes process and workflows to build stronger client trust.
